episodes.title: The $115 Billion Question
episodes.dek: Nvidia just posted its biggest quarter ever, five days after its founder-CEO resigned.

tiles.alt: Dre, in a barber chair, turns to Scoop as he walks into the shop with a tablet while Unc holds clippers. Dre: Scoop! Nvidia's CEO stepped down. They finished, right? Scoop: Not even close, young man. Title: The $115 Billion Question.
Scoop shows a rising bar chart to a stunned Unc and Dre. Scoop: Five days later, they reported $115.8 billion. In one quarter. Unc: Billion? With a B?!
Keys explains from the waiting bench with her laptop. Keys: $107.6 billion of it is data centers. Every AI company is buying their chips. Scoop: Gold rush. Nvidia sells the shovels.
A thoughtful Scoop with Unc behind him under an orange neon scissors sign. Unc: So the money's right. But who's driving the bus? Scoop: The CFO, for now. The board is still searching for a new CEO.
Unc spreads his arms over his busy shop. Unc: I tell my barbers: if this shop can't run without me, I don't own a business... Scoop: ...you own a job. Wall Street calls it key-person risk.
Dre holds up his phone as Scoop laughs and Miss Pearl peers over her glasses. Dre: Say less. I'm buying Nvidia tonight! Miss Pearl: Baby, you still owe Unc for last week's cut.
SHOP TALK end card with Scoop's portrait and the cast. Sources and the full breakdown at hicksnewmedia.com/shoptalk. Shop the merch at merch.hicksnewmedia.com.

facts: Revenue: $115.8B for the quarter ended Oct 25, up 103% from a year ago.
Data center: $107.6B, up 110%. That's about 93% of Nvidia's sales.
Leadership: Jensen Huang resigned Nov 12. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO; the board says it will not reinstate Huang.
Outlook: Q4 guided to $130B (±3%), with no China data center compute revenue assumed. FY28 growth outlook raised to about 75%.
episodes.why: Record results during a leadership vacuum tell you the product and the customers are strong. They don't tell you who sets the next five-year bet. That's key-person risk, and it applies to a trillion-dollar chipmaker and a four-chair barbershop the same way.

episodes.title: Is That Deal Real?
episodes.dek: Black Friday's done. Cyber Monday's coming. The shop checks the receipts.
facts: Groundwork Collaborative checked 351 items from Amazon's Black Friday and Cyber Monday deal pages in 2024 and 2025: 29.1% were priced the same or higher than in the month before, and nearly 60% against the prior 90 days. Amazon calls the study flawed and says 98% were at or below their 30-day price.
Price tracker Visualping found about 1 in 3 Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals in 2025 had been cheaper earlier in the season. Game consoles were the safest bet (14%); luggage the riskiest (61%).
Adobe forecasts a record $21.3B in buy now, pay later spending this holiday season, including $1.09B on Cyber Monday (Nov 30).
Adobe forecasts electronics as the season's biggest online category at $63.3B, and expects Black Friday to bring the biggest TV discounts.

verdict.text: Until you check. Cop only if the price beats the item's 90-day low. Look up the price history, compare at least three stores, and pay in full if you can.

episodes.why: The crossed-out price is marketing. The price history is the fact. Retailers set the "was" price, so a percent off tells you nothing until you know what the item actually sold for. Black Friday can be a real low for TVs. The only way to know is to check.

tiles.alt: Weekend Edition cover. Saturday morning at the shop: Dre walks in hugging a big TV box with shopping bags while Unc turns in his barber chair and Miss Pearl lowers her newspaper. Unc: Here comes Black Friday himself. Dre: Y'all! 75-inch TV. 40% off! Title: Is That Deal Real?

Keys turns her laptop toward Dre to show a flat price chart; his grin drops. Keys: Forty percent off a price it never sold for. Dre: So I got got? Fact: 29.1% of Amazon's featured 2024 to 2025 Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals were no cheaper than a month earlier. Amazon disputes it.

Scoop holds up his tablet with a line chart. Scoop: Not yet. The slashed price is the hook. The price history is the truth. Fact: Visualping found about 1 in 3 Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals in 2025 had been cheaper earlier in the season.

Unc peers over his glasses at Dre's phone showing four payment blocks; Dre rubs his neck. Unc: Young man, four easy payments is still the whole price. Fact: Adobe forecasts a record 21.3 billion dollars in buy now, pay later spending this season, 1.09 billion on Cyber Monday alone.

Keys points at the shop TV while Scoop nods and Dre hugs his TV box with relief. Keys: Good news: that's its 90-day low. Dre: So I didn't get got! Fact: Adobe forecasts electronics as the season's top online category at 63.3 billion dollars, with Black Friday bringing the deepest TV discounts.

The verdict. Miss Pearl peers over her glasses as Dre holds a long receipt. A stamp reads WAIT, till you check. Miss Pearl: Baby, sit down. Check the price, not the percent. Dre: Yes ma'am. Cop only if it beats the item's 90-day low.
